newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin lays ground for U.S.-Russia summit.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin lays ground for U.S.-Russia summit.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has prepared a long awaited new cabinet line-up and on Saturday laid the economic groundwork for Boris Yeltsin's Helsinki summit with Bill Clinton, his spokesman said.
Viktor Konnov said Chernomyrdin held three hours of talks with U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers in the Russian government's White House headquarters.

He said the accent was on Russia's integration into world economic systems and admission into organisations like the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and Paris Club of government creditors.
The two men also discussed the Denver summit of the Group of Seven, the club of big industrial democracies.

U.S. officials have said Russia would get enhanced membership of the G-7 by the June summit but Moscow is pressing to become a full member of the club and the other organisations and clearly hopes Helsinki will bring a breakthrough.
Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yaztrzhembsky said on Saturday that Washington should do more to help promote Moscow's case.
"In this very area the role of the United States is invaluable and and it is here that this country could show greater cooperation with Russia," Interfax news agency quoted Yastrzhembsky as saying.

Konnov gave no details of the results of Saturday's talks, which are aimed at preparing the way for Yeltsin's meetings with Clinton in Finland next week, where the controversial issue of NATO expansion is expected to head the agenda.
They take place against a background of deep uncertainty for Russia's cabinet, after Yeltsin's announcement more than a week ago that there would be a far-reaching reshuffle.
Details have yet to emerge but Konnov said Chernomyrdin had finished drawing up his proposals. "I think that Chernomyrdin has done his part of the job," he said by telephone.
Asked when an announcment might take place, he referred to media interviews Yeltsin is due to give on Monday ahead of the summit, adding: "No doubt he will announce everything himself."
The Kremlin said on Friday that an announcement would be made before Yeltsin heads for Finland on Wednesday.

Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, who is expected to survive the reshuffle, left for Washington on Saturday seeking to prepare for a deal with the U.S. president that could lead to a compromise on NATO's expansion plans.
The foreign ministry has said Primakov has proposals to make in the row with NATO over its plans to offer membership to Moscow's former communist allies in eastern and central Europe.
Primakov, who meets Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Saturday, Defence Secretary William Cohen on Sunday and Clinton on Monday, also expects serious discussion on arms control.

Helsinki will be a chance for Yeltsin, 66, to show he has recovered after eight months of heart trouble and pneumonia. He even got the chance to turn the tables and send get well wishes to Clinton, who had an operation on his injured knee on Friday.

The Kremlin leader, who says he is determined to take Russia's international and domestic problems in hand, said on Friday the March 19-20 summit would be his toughest ever but that compromise was possible.
There may also be compromise -- this time between Russia's reformers and Yeltsin's more conservative allies -- in Yeltsin's new government team.

But the time taken to form the new government since he handed a leading role a week ago to his liberal chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais has fuelled speculation that cutting out dead wood and creating a streamlined pro-reform team is proving hard.

Indications from Yeltsin that the upper ranks of the cabinet may be fuller than expected was also seen by some analysts as a sign he may be slow to alienate faithful supporters for the sake of the new approach Chubais is believed to be seeking.
Yeltsin said on Friday there would, in addition to Chubais as sole first deputy premier, be seven deputy premiers. There are three first deputies and nine deputies in the present team.
